claim: A boundary wall, a building's low range or a pitched nave that must look lower than what stands beyond it is a sector whose FLOOR is its top, under the common sky; its face is the lower step of a two-sided wall and the view passes over it. Over an interior it is a second layer, with a band clear of the rooms beneath.
evidence: projects/blood-city/experiments/church-roofs: a 3.1-body wall with nothing behind it, a 3.9-body range over an interior and a 5.8-7.0 sloped nave all read; skies lowered a body or more went from 5 to 0; a blind reviewer went from 'cemetery wall (guess)' to 'graveyard (certain)'
use: skyline.roof, then skyline.dress_steps so the face wears a tile from the side that sees it.
